newsitem.title: FRANCE: French culture minister slashed on election trip.
newsitem.headline: French culture minister slashed on election trip.

text.p: French Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy was slashed on Friday afternoon by a knife-wielding assailant during an election campaign trip to Lourdes in southwestern France.
Douste-Blazy was rushed to hospital but his injury, a knife cut in the back, was not life-threatening, doctors at the Lourdes hospital said in a statement.
A man was captured shortly after the stabbing and was being held for questioning. "It was a man from the area who was mentally unstable," a police source said.

"Mr Douste-Blazy's life is not in danger and his health does not appear to be cause for serious worry," the statement said. "He was struck in the back, between the shoulder blades, but no vital organ seems to have been hit."
Douste-Blazy was attacked with a jacknife at about 6.30 p.m. (1630 GMT) while touring a souvenir shop, unescorted, on a central Lourdes street, a spokesman for city hall said.
His recovery was expected to take about 10 days.

Douste-Blazy is mayor of Lourdes, renowned throughout the Catholic world for its grotto and springs which the religion's followers believe contain healing waters. The attack took place several hundred metres from any holy sites.
Douste-Blazy, a former health minister and himself a medical doctor, was campaigning for a two-round parliamentary election set for May 25-June 1.
The suspected assailant was arrested in a cafe near the scene of the attack, where he had ordered a cold drink. Witnesses said he offered no resistance when taken into custody.
Police did not give his name, but said he was born in 1960 and was under psychological care. Police said the man had offered no reason for the attack.
Marie-Noelle Toulouse, owner of the store in which the attack took place, said Douste-Blazy entered the store and approached her to shake hands.
The assailant followed the minister in, walked straight up to him and stabbed him forcefully in the back, she said.
He then dropped the knife and ran out of the store, Toulouse said. She said Douste-Blazy never lost consciousness and said to her: "It's ok, my heart wasn't hit."
She said she went outside, stopped a passing car and had the mayor driven to the hospital.
Politicians were united in their condemnation of the attack.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe called for calm and said he hoped the attack was not politically motivated. "I hope the campaign will steer clear of such outbursts, that every one will keep his cool," he said while campaigning in nearby Bordeaux.
"My thoughts are with Philippe and I hope he will recover soon," Juppe added.
Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin censured the attack. "I was shocked to hear of this...and I offer him my sympathy and solidarity. I hope he recovers quickly."
